item.title: Skiing in China was once a luxury. Local manufacturers are slashing costs
item.description: Skiing has long been considered an expensive sport in China, with the industry heavily reliant on imported specialised equipment and machinery for resorts. But domestic manufacturers are beginning to reshape the market by offering cheaper alternatives while also expanding overseas. The shift is already visible at indoor ski centres in Shenzhen, where locally made equipment is increasingly being used for ski lessons and rental services. “Domestic equipment has improved rapidly and is particularly...

item.title: Is the US reviving Subic Bay in the Philippines as an ‘unbranded military base’?
item.description: The United States is quietly transforming Subic Bay in the Philippines back into an “unbranded military base” that could support US operations in both the South China Sea and the Taiwan Strait, according to a Chinese think tank. item.title: Major storm batters US on Thanksgiving holiday, disrupting flights and power
item.description: A powerful storm disrupted Thanksgiving celebrations for millions of Americans on Thursday, as New York’s famed Macy’s parade was postponed for the first time in its 100-year history. Heavy rain and strong winds from the “Nor-easter” battered the central and eastern United States, creating treacherous travel conditions during one of the country’s busiest holiday periods. item.title: AI is changing child exploitation. Our response must change too
item.description: Artificial intelligence is giving offenders new ways to exploit children. Images of real children can be AI-manipulated into sexual abuse material, while chatbots allow users to rehearse abusive encounters and, in some cases, obtain guidance on grooming. These systems can also help offenders construct convincing false identities and tailor messages to gain a young person’s trust, raising the prospect of grooming more children with less time and effort.
